To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we developed a new method of automatically coding human behavioral interaction data using speech acoustic features, (b) we applied the method to a large corpus of problem-solving interactions of married couples, and (c) we obtained significant improvements in the classification accuracy of the selected codes over our previously reported results.

we have developed a new automated system for coding behavioral data that outperforms previous systems and that we have demonstrated the feasibility of using automatic systems to code behavioral observations in intimate relationships.

we were able to automatically classify extreme behavioral instances of six selected codes using acoustic features, and that the best overall automatic system classified 74.2% of the instances correctly, an improvement of about 4% absolute (6% relative) over the best previous system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) How can we automatically classify extreme behavioral observations for married couples’ problem solving interactions from audio recordings? and 2) What are the relative contributions of prosody, spectral, and vocal quality features to the automatic coding of behavioral observations?
the following question: Can speech acoustic features be used to automatically predict behavioral codes in a human behavioral data set?
the development of a computational method for the analysis and prediction of human behavior.
